claims.text: Catalytic activity of nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalysts for ethanol oxidation is governed by electronic-structure modulation caused by atomic-scale lattice distortions.
Atomic-scale lattice distortions alter the adsorption energies of ethanol and its oxidation intermediates.
The initial PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is nanoscale, solid-solution, and atomically homogeneous.
Thermal treatment or substrate-induced strain can controllably modulate atomic-scale lattice distortions in the catalyst.
Lattice distortions modify the d-band center of the constituent metal atoms.
Changes in the d-band center affect the adsorption energies of ethanol and its oxidation intermediates.
Changes in adsorption energies influence ethanol-oxidation catalytic activity.
Increasing lattice strain will cause a measurable change in catalytic current density relative to an unstrained catalyst.
Catalytic activity will depend nonlinearly on the degree of lattice strain.
The baseline is an unstrained PtPdRhRuIrOs solid-solution catalyst tested under otherwise identical reaction conditions.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold for lattice strains between -5% and +5%.
The proposed relationship is expected to hold in acidic aqueous electrolyte at 60–80 degrees Celsius during ethanol oxidation.
Strain-induced segregation or phase separation may compete with the proposed electronic effect.
A lack of correlation or significant activity change across controlled strain levels would falsify the hypothesis.
